conventions.convention: Geometry is smooth, Hausdorff, second-countable and boundaryless in dimension four, with signature (−,+,+,+), independent manifold orientation, time orientation and the metric-selected Levi–Civita connection. Countable Choice is inherited through the geometric suppliers.
The Hodge star satisfies α ∧ ⋆β = ⟨α,β⟩g vol_g and ⋆² = −id on two-forms.

The sourced convention is ∇a F^{ab} = −μ₀j^b, equivalent to d(⋆F) = μ₀ i_j vol_g. In positive normal coordinates E_i = −cF_{0i}, B_i = ε_{ijk}F_{jk}/2, ε₁₂₃ = +1 and ∂t = c∂₀. Normal-coordinate derivatives act on chart-component abbreviations.

Connection variations remain in one fixed normalized circle-bundle sector: transition maps stay fixed, global physical one-form directions α are allowed and δF = dα. The normalization κ₀ is positive and is not identified with electric charge or Planck's constant.

Variations are smooth families fixed outside one common compact set. Noncompact action variations mean finite compactly supported action differences. Metric variation holds lower F components fixed and uses q^{ab} = δg^{ab} with δS = −(2c)⁻¹ ∫T_ab q^{ab} vol_g.

Chains are finite formal real combinations of smoothly extendible singular simplices, with signed face boundary. Charge is Q(Σ) = c⁻¹ ∫Σ i_j vol_g; boundary decomposition ∂C = Σ₂ − Σ₁ + B gives Q(Σ₂) − Q(Σ₁) = −Q(B).
The spatial torus is R³/(L₁Z × L₂Z × L₃Z), with all L_i > 0. Product orientation is dx⁰ ∧ dx¹ ∧ dx² ∧ dx³ and future direction is ∂₀.

Observer components use a positively oriented orthonormal tetrad with E₀ = n. Geometric normalization uses α = √(4πG_N/(μ₀c⁴)), the positive root, and ℱ = αF; SI assignments are formal dimensional bookkeeping.

load_bearing.statement: For smooth F and j on the specified oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, with μ₀,c > 0, define v^b = ∇a F^{ab}. Then d(⋆F) = −i_v vol_g, hence ∇a F^{ab} = −μ₀j^b iff d(⋆F) = μ₀ i_j vol_g. Either sourced equation implies ∇a j^a = 0 without requiring dF = 0. The stated normal-coordinate component identities give the four Maxwell equations in the additional fixed inertial Minkowski specialization.

Under the specified fixed-bundle connection interface and compact-support hypotheses, δ_A S_EM[α] = (μ₀c)⁻¹ ∫(∇a F^{ab})α_b vol_g. With the hypothesized matter first variation c⁻¹∫j^bα_b vol_g, stationarity for every admissible compactly supported α is equivalent to ∇a F^{ab} = −μ₀j^b. Compact inverse-metric variation at fixed lower F gives T_EM,ab = μ₀⁻¹(F_ac F_b{}^c − g_ab F_cd F^{cd}/4), excluding source/matter stress.

For smooth F,j satisfying dF = 0 and ∇a F^{ab} = −μ₀j^b, with c,μ₀ > 0, every finite smooth singular three-chain satisfies Q(Σ) = (μ₀c)⁻¹∫∂Σ ⋆F. Thus ∂Σ = 0 implies Q(Σ) = 0. Every bounding magnetic flux ∫∂V F vanishes, and ∂C = Σ₂ − Σ₁ + B implies Q(Σ₂) − Q(Σ₁) = −Q(B). No noncompact limiting conclusion is asserted.

Under its geometric and conditional variational hypotheses, the displayed Maxwell tensor is symmetric and trace-free; its positive observer tetrad components are the stated quadratic electric/magnetic formulas, with T^{0i} = (E × B)_i/(μ₀c). Observer energy density is nonnegative and S_n has spatial components (E × B)_i/μ₀. For Q_g(H)_ab = H_ac H_b{}^c − g_ab H_cd H^{cd}/4, Q_g(λH) = λ²Q_g(H), and ℱ = √(4πG_N/(μ₀c⁴))F gives κ_E T_EM = 2Q_g(ℱ).

For positive real periods L₁,L₂,L₃, R³/(L₁Z × L₂Z × L₃Z) is a compact Hausdorff second-countable smooth boundaryless three-manifold, and its quotient map is a smooth local diffeomorphism. Coordinate forms, coordinate vector fields and smooth periodic functions descend. The stated product Lorentzian geometry is smooth, with constant metric components and vanishing metric-selected Christoffel symbols in product quotient charts.

concerns.concern: The Remarks say: “The sign $T_{\mathrm{EM}}^{0i}>0$ is for the conventions”. This literal positivity claim is false: part (b) correctly gives T^{0i} = (E × B)_i/(μ₀c), which can be negative or zero. For example E = (1,0,0), B = (0,−1,0) gives T^{03} < 0, while F = 0 gives zero. The issue is confined to this remark; the displayed tensor formulas and their derivation have the correct relative signs.

Fact F8 attributes to def-integral-of-a-form-over-a-smooth-singular-simplex that “it also establishes that T_3 is compact Jordan”; verification step 2.3 then cites this attribution. The opened definition specifies T_k and defines the integral as a Jordan-set Riemann integral, but supplies no compactness/Jordan-measurability argument. This is an immediate missing justification: T_3 is closed and bounded and has boundary in finitely many bounded affine-plane pieces, so the Heine–Borel and content-zero graph/boundary arguments already used later in step 2.3 apply. The attribution should identify an actual supplier or state that argument locally.

seams_checked.note: Read the normalized connection definition and gluing statement/proof against the action and stress uses. Fixed transition maps permit global base one-form differences; scaling the normalized difference by κ₀ gives the physical α and δF = dα. Draft status, normalization and absence of a global-potential assumption are preserved.

Both physical consumers retain smooth field domains, the negative tensor-source convention, positive normal-chart component abbreviations, finite chains, charge factor 1/c, cycle neutrality and the side-flux condition. Their additional physical adoption is explicit and is not attributed to the mathematical suppliers.

The Einstein-action consumer uses compact relative action variation at fixed lower F with the exact −1/(2c) stress convention. The Maxwell-divergence consumer uses the same tensor and source sign. The matter Noether item uses the current lemma only to match the downstream source convention and explicitly does not assume Maxwell equations in its own deduction.

RN and KN verification consumers use clause (d)'s quadratic scaling with α = √(4πG_N/(μ₀c⁴)) and κ_E T = 2Q_g(ℱ). They explicitly define the algebraic tensor and preserve the separate fixed-sector hypotheses for its Hilbert-tensor interpretation; arbitrary geometric flux is not asserted to admit a circle-bundle realization.
